name: The Gilded Spark

detectability.signature: A searing point-source of gold-white radiation with harmonic spikes in bands no natural process produces; long-range arrays flag it before it is visible to the eye.

proximity: Faster-than-light drives spool up unbidden and must be physically locked out
Crew report a metallic taste and vivid, shared dreams of vast moving distances
contact: Hull metal transmutes a few atoms deep into stable gold isotopes
Any active jump drive is fused into permanent alignment with the bleed
prolonged_exposure: Matter in the core region begins phasing between reference frames; solid objects become arguments
Biological tissue desynchronizes from local spacetime with outcomes best described as non-recoverable

phenomena: The bleed's light is visibly golden, unlike any natural emission spectrum on record
Ghost images of ships that never arrived flicker at its edge for fractions of a second
Instruments within a light-second disagree about the anomaly's size, by factors that change hourly
hazards: Uncommanded FTL events capable of tearing a ship apart mid-spool
Lethal exotic radiation with no practical shielding
Spacetime desynchronization in the inner volume; three research drones sent in have not come back and also never stopped transmitting
opportunities: The gold-atom surface conversion has made the boundary debris field the richest salvage ground in the sector
Bleed harmonics are the only known calibration source for next-generation jump drives
known_incidents: The Spark was born when the experimental jump liner Meridian Queen misfolded with nine hundred souls aboard; the ship has never been found, but every year on the anniversary her engines are heard spooling somewhere inside.
A corporate salvage flotilla ignored the exclusion radius twelve years ago; the two hulls that drifted out were plated in gold and crewed by no one.
description: The Gilded Spark burns like a tiny furious star: an irregular knot of gold-white light barely a hundredth of an astronomical unit across, visible from a dozen systems away on clear sensors. Its spectrum matches nothing natural. Around it drifts a slow halo of debris — hull plates, drive rings, personal effects — each item gilded at the surface as if dipped, glittering as it tumbles.

The Spark does not sit still so much as argue with itself, contracting in lurches with no cycle anyone has extracted. Approach it and drives wake without permission; touch its boundary and matter comes away changed; enter the inner volume and physics files a formal complaint. The contraction rate suggests the whole structure will collapse to nothing within another century, though the estimate has been revised upward four times.

It has an origin, which makes it rare among extreme anomalies: this is the scar of the Meridian Queen, the jump liner that folded wrong three centuries ago with nine hundred passengers aboard. The exclusion zone went up within a year. The salvage rush came anyway, drawn by the gilded debris, and the flotilla disaster ended the argument about whether the zone was advisory. Since then the Spark has been studied at range, mourned at distance, and robbed only by the brave and the patient.

Current research focuses on the ghost images: frames of ships that never existed, or that have not arrived yet, depending on which physicist you ask. The contraction continues. The Meridian Queen's engines are still heard, always on the anniversary, always just inside the boundary. And the salvage rights to whatever remains when the Spark finally closes are the most contested piece of paper in the sector.
